name: East Staffordshire

licensing.selective: Selective licensing on nine streets in central Burton upon Trent (including Branston Road, Shobnall Street, Queen Street and Waterloo Street), from 12 September 2022 to 11 September 2027. In February 2026 the council consulted on renewing it and covering 16 streets.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: only mandatory licensing, for HMOs with five or more people from two or more households.

housing: East Staffordshire is centred on Burton upon Trent, a brewing town with large areas of Victorian terraced housing, and the market town of Uttoxeter, with villages across a rural north. Private lets in Burton are mostly older terraces and flats near the town centre, alongside new-build estates on the edges. Some terraced streets in central Burton have been converted to shared housing. Homes near the Trent and Dove are in areas at risk of flooding.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in central Burton: photograph back yards, rear outbuildings, damp at the base of walls and the condition of windows and doors.
Shared houses in Burton: photograph each bedroom and its lock, the shared kitchen and fire doors, and note the key count for each room.
Homes near the Trent and Dove: photograph any damp tide marks, air bricks and flood barriers left for the tenant.
New-build estates around Burton and Uttoxeter: photograph snagging marks and meter readings, and note any estate management charges or parking rules.
Rural cottages off the gas grid: photograph the oil tank, its gauge and level, and the boiler service label.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact East Staffordshire Borough Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect rented homes and take action against landlords.
